ArgumentParser.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initialize the instance state by assigning fresh empty containers for arguments, required items, and type mappings." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign self.arguments to a new empty dictionary to establish an initially empty argument mapping. RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Assign self.required to a new empty set to establish an initially empty collection of required items. RESULT self.required]
            [COMMAND Assign self.types to a new empty dictionary to establish an initially empty type mapping. RESULT self.types]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.parse_arguments:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Parse command-line style arguments into a dictionary, converting typed values, handling boolean flags, and returning missing required arguments when any are absent." parse_arguments]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split the command string on whitespace and discard the first token to obtain the argument list. RESULT args]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over each index i in the full range from 0 to len(args) - 1, read the current token args[i] and classify it by prefix. RESULT arg]
            [COMMAND If the current token starts with '--', remove the leading dashes, split the remainder on '=', and treat the token as a long option. RESULT key_value]
            [COMMAND Within the long-option branch, if the split produces exactly two parts, store the first part as the key and the converted second part as the value in self.arguments. RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Within the long-option branch, if the split does not produce exactly two parts, store the first part as a boolean True flag in self.arguments. RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Else if the current token starts with '-', remove the leading dash and treat the token as a short option. RESULT key]
            [COMMAND Within the short-option branch, if i + 1 is still within bounds and the next token does not start with '-', consume the next token as this option's value and store its converted form in self.arguments. RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Within the short-option branch, if no valid value token follows, store the short option key as a boolean True flag in self.arguments. RESULT self.arguments]
            [COMMAND Compute the set difference between self.required and the keys currently present in self.arguments to determine which required arguments are missing. RESULT missing_args]
            [COMMAND If any required arguments are missing, return False together with the missing argument set. RESULT (False, missing_args)]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, return True together with None to indicate successful parsing. RESULT (True, None)]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.get_argument:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Retrieve the value associated with the given key from the instance arguments mapping, returning the mapping's default missing-key result when the key is absent." get_argument]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> key </REF>: any "Key used to look up a value in the instance arguments mapping."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "Value stored for the key in self.arguments, or the default result of dict.get when the key is not present, which is None when no explicit default is provided."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read the value for the provided key from self.arguments using the mapping get operation without supplying an explicit default. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return the retrieved result. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser.add_argument:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Conditionally records an argument as required and stores its type in the instance type mapping under that argument key." add_argument]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance that owns the required-argument collection and the type mapping."
        <REF> arg </REF>: any "Argument identifier to register in the instance state."
        <REF> required </REF>: bool "Flag indicating whether the argument should be marked as required; defaults to false."
        <REF> arg_type </REF>: type "Type or type-like value to associate with the argument; defaults to str."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND If required is true, add arg to self.required. RESULT self.required updated conditionally]
            [COMMAND Assign arg_type into self.types using arg as the key, overwriting any existing value for that key. RESULT self.types[arg]]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArgumentParser._convert_type:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts the given value using the converter registered for the specified argument key, and falls back to returning the original value if conversion is not possible." _convert_type]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> arg </REF>: any "Key used to select a converter from the types mapping."
        <REF> value </REF>: any "Input value to convert."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "Converted value, or the original value if conversion fails or the key is missing."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Look up the converter function in self.types using arg and apply it to value. RESULT converted_value]
            [COMMAND Return the converted value. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: If the lookup or conversion raises ValueError or KeyError.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the original value without modification. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
